plan_a_advantages: Maintains a high volume of easy trail running, potentially beneficial for maintaining trail-specific fitness.
Offers a consistent, predictable schedule with minimal variation.
plan_b_advantages: Includes a tempo run, directly addressing speed development.
Incorporates strength and mobility work, crucial for injury prevention and performance enhancement in trail running.
Provides a more balanced approach to training, combining aerobic and strength elements.
reasoning: Plan B is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While Plan A focuses almost exclusively on easy trail running, which can be beneficial for maintaining freshness, it lacks any structured efforts to build speed or improve aerobic capacity beyond the easy runs. Plan B incorporates a tempo run, crucial for developing sustainable threshold strength – a key component of faster trail running – and includes dedicated strength and mobility work to support durability and injury prevention. The consistent easy aerobic runs in Plan B also provide a solid foundation for building endurance, which is essential for tackling longer trail distances.
